meaningMnemonic: You see something with a little flag next to it and put it in your mouth. It was spicy! You look at the little flag and it says...hot. You just ate a hot pepper .

There's an explosion around your legs. It was just as the fortune teller warned. This is the omen she was talking about. Think about what happens after the omen hits. What horrible fortune teller magic will happen???
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means prize .
There's a stick going through some juicy meat. This is a skewer .
This radical is the same as the kanji. It means violence .
Yourself (oneself) is in prison. Look at the prison as it wraps around you. It wraps you up and holds you tight. That's why this is the wrap radical!

A skewer to the heart has afflicted your health. You’ve been afflicted with a disease from the skewer to your heart. Your affliction is death. You’re dying. Hints You did not wish to be afflicted as such. Feel the skewer in your heart and the great pain it gives you. You know you’re dying.
readingMnemonic: Since you’re afflicted with the death, you start to hallucinate and the ghost of Genghis Khan ( かん ) appears before you. "Ah, I was afflicted of the same disease. meaningMnemonic: You see an animal wearing a top hat and decide to aim at it. The top hat is a perfect, giant target you use to take down this animal. Hints It's much easier to aim for an animal wearing a top hat than one without.
readingMnemonic: Ready, steady, aim ... fire! You throw a bar of so ap ( そ ) at the animal. Yes, soap. You were sitting in your bathtub, washing and scrubbing, then the animal in the top hat caught your eye. Hints Your aim with the soap is perfect! The soap knocked the animal's hat right off.

meaningMnemonic: This building is full of car s because it's an army camp . The cars (and tanks and planes) need to be ready to go at any moment just like the soldiers. Hints Picture an army camp housing all of the different cars the army needs at any given time.
readingMnemonic: All of the people in the army camp are wearing jean s ( じん ). You thought soldiers were supposed to wear uniforms, but it looks like when they're in the camp they have to wear jeans. Hints Jeans are pretty durable, now that you think about it. And if the soldiers are working on these cars in the camp while they're there, it makes sense to wear a nice pair of jeans.

meaningMnemonic: Under the rice paddy , an explosion shakes the dirt , exposing a hidden base . A baseball base ! I guess this rice paddy was built on top of an old baseball field… Hints Picture a serene rice paddy. Now watch the whole thing explode, rice and dirt going everywhere, and a secret, underground baseball base is left there, smoldering.
readingMnemonic: Unfortunately, thanks to the explosion, the base is in rui ns ( るい ). It's dark and smokey and kinda half burned. You probably can't get this in a regulation game. Hints Hold this ruined baseball base in your hands. Hey, maybe it's a collectible?

meaningMnemonic: What's like a bow , but even more simple ? A bullet . With a bow, you have to load an arrow and pull back the string and aim, yuck. Bullets can be shot with just a simple squeeze of a trigger. Hints Imagine how simple life would be if we replaced all the bows in the world with bullets. (Insert sarcastic crying face here.)
readingMnemonic: If you want to shoot bullet s, you need to do it at dawn ( だん ). Back in the old days, it wasn't bright enough to shoot arrows at dawn, but you can shoot bullets at dawn because they're simpler to use! Hints Imagine shooting bullets into the sun at dawn. Pow pow, take that history! Blam blam, take that dawn!

meaningMnemonic: You brought flowers to leave at the place where a yakuza took a spoon and killed twenty people, since there's now a burial happening there. You didn't know these people, but you still want to leave flowers at their burial. Hints Give a yakuza a spoon and you always get 死 (death), in this case twenty times. So it's honestly not surprising that things would end with commemorative flowers and a burial.
readingMnemonic: Once the burial is complete the sou ls ( そう ) of all the dead people come floating up and out of the ground. "Thaaannk YooOoOO~" they moan, as they ascend to the sky. Hints I guess the twenty souls couldn't go up to... wherever... until they had a proper burial.

meaningMnemonic: You take your fingers and slam a lid on the table . You make this big noise to confront the person in front of you. Hints They weren't listening, which is why you slammed that lid down. You'll have to confront them more directly.
readingMnemonic: You are trying to confront Emperor こう いち . You're confronting him about all the kanji he's forcing you, and everyone else, to learn. "Look here こういち ! I know you said I'd learn like 2000 kanji in no time, but this is way too efficient! What will the people do when they're done? Do you think they will sit idly by?" Hints こういち is laughing at you as you confront him. Which makes you angrier, so you bang the lid on the table some more.

meaningMnemonic: Below this mountain , a moon and another moon crash into each other and the entire thing crumble s to pieces. Hints Watch as the moons crumble together, and then the mountain slowly crumbles down into them too.
readingMnemonic: As the mountain crumble s you see your ho me ( ほう ), which is at the very top of the mountain, come crumbling down too. Hints Your home crumbles like a dry cookie until it's nothing more than a bunch of dust, mixed in with the mountain and the moon. Now where will you live?

meaningMnemonic: On the scooter is an insect and a bear . The bear immediately stomps the insect, squishing it flat. "My god, the insect is smashed. Someone call dispatch !" Hints Imagine the conversation with emergency services. They say they will dispatch an ambulance immediately.
readingMnemonic: Out of the dispatch ed ambulance jumps Ken ( けん ) the samurai. "Dispatch sent me! I'm here to fix that insect." Hints He takes out a very tiny katana and performs surgery right there. The insect dies on the scooter. "It looks like I've dispatched this insect to the afterlife."

meaningMnemonic: Use your fingers when the sun shines into your prison cell and hold your spoon up in full display . Hints Picture the sun reflecting off your metal prison spoon as you hold it aloft in your fingers. It hurts your eyes a little, but it also draws everyone's attention to this spoon you want to display.
readingMnemonic: The reason you display it is to get some ca ke ( けい ). In this prison, if you display your spoon deftly enough, the wardens bring you some cake as a reward. Hints It's gotta be a spoon because forks are too pointy and dangerous for prison, by the way. So imagine eating your cake with the spoon you just displayed, big spoonfuls of cake frosting filling your mouth with every bite.

meaningMnemonic: If you combine fire with violence , it will explode ! A fire, once full of violence, will surely explode. The fire can’t handle all that violence so the fire just rumbles and shakes and then finally explodes. BOOM! Hints Imagine the fire explode. Feel the heat of the fire and the explosion. It’s very violent. BOOM BOOM BA-BOOM!
readingMnemonic: As you watch the fire explode , you start to back ( ばく ) away. I don’t blame you. You need to back away or else you’ll get caught in the violent explosion. Back away a little more just to be safe. Hints Imagine yourself as you back away from the explosion. As you back away, see the fire dance and feel the heat of the explosion on your face.

meaningMnemonic: You're holding a flag on a stick above your eye s to imitate eyebrows . You can't grow any of your own, but you really love eyebrows, so this was the best you could do. Hints Look at yourself in the mirror. You can see the stick holding up the flag and it's very clear you drew some eyebrows onto the flag with some markers, but you still look pretty good (in your opinion).
readingMnemonic: Underneath your fake eyebrows are two slabs of me at ( み ). Meat helps hair grow, according to many Internet specialists who also happen to sell meat. You're waiting for this meat to foster eyebrow hair, and when that sweet day comes you won't need these flags. Hints Imagine walking around town, holding your eyebrow flags. You can feel the meat sticking above your eyes. They stink and they're weirdly lukewarm, but you know your real eyebrows will grow under them any day now.

meaningMnemonic: You carry a cross across a rice paddy with a heart on it to return a favor for your friend. The heart needs to be purified so that’s why you have it on the cross and your friend lives on a rice paddy farm so that’s why you’re running through that. The favor you are paying your friend back with is getting him this heart. He needs a new one and you’re providing it. Hints This is a pretty big favor. Imagine running through a rice paddy carrying a cross with a warm beating heart on it. Thump thump. Thump thump.
readingMnemonic: You arrive at your friend’s place and you can finally return the favor you owe him by presenting him with the heart. “ Eh ( え )? What’s this? I didn’t ask for this!” “Eh!?!?” you reply. Apparently he didn’t want a real heart, he wanted a candy one. He wanted a Valentine! Hints Imagine how dumb you feel at this miscommunication. Eh? You don’t feel dumb? Well you should!

meaningMnemonic: At this gate you're trying to get some beans through, but your measurements were off, leading to a big fight . The bean authorities at the gate always want to fight about bean sizes, and now you have to fight to get those beans through. Hints Imagine having to fight against the bean bureaucracy. It's so absurd! Who can say a bean is too big or too small, in this age of diversity?! Your fighting pays off though, and they let you squeeze your beans through the gate. Well fought, bean brethren. Well fought.
readingMnemonic: The gate you put up a fight at leads to とう きょう . The people of とうきょう need those beans for sustenance, and that's why you fight — for them! Hints How are you supposed to get your beans into とうきょう if a fight breaks out at the gate every time? What a struggle. Fortunately those bean-counting bureaucrats of とうきょう were no match for your fight.

meaningMnemonic: A tsunami pushes all the fish closer to land, making for some easy fishing . The tsunami starts out in the middle of the ocean and pushes all the fish towards the coast where everyone does their fishing. With all the fish pushed closer to land and closer together, it’s very easy for people to go fishing in one spot and catch a lot of fish. Hints Imagine going fishing for fish in a fishing spot after a tsunami. There are SO many fish here. Your hook barely touches the water and there’s already a fish on it. Man, fishing like this is easy! Smell the smell of fish and sea air around you.
readingMnemonic: To get to the best fishing spot you need to go ( ぎょ ) row ( りょう ) out to the middle of the ocean. You go by means of rowing. To get to the fish and do the fishing, you need to go and row out to sea. Hints Go! Go row! Go and row for the fishing! How do you go? You row! The row part should be pretty easy to remember since you gotta row your boat out to sea, but if you’re having trouble with the go part, just remember that it has the same reading as 魚 .

meaningMnemonic: Grain left in the sun blossom and give off a wonderful fragrance . They smell fresh and delicious. There's nothing better than the fragrance of fresh, sun-kissed grain. readingMnemonic: As you sniff this lovely fragrance you get lost in the smell. When you open your eyes again, you see a farming こう いち standing in front of you. With... his... arm... up. "Do you like my fragrance? I was genetically modified to have a unique fragrance compared to the other こういち s." Hints This fragrance was こういち 's armpits the whole time. You thought it was warm grains. Or... maybe he smells like... grains?

meaningMnemonic: Tsunami s hit these lands again and again, molding it into some kind of bow shape. Or in other words, creating a gulf . Hints Picture these extremely violent tsunamis hitting a shore again and again, turning it into a bow-shaped gulf. That's how gulfs are created in this part of the world!
readingMnemonic: How many gulf s will this create? Just one ( わん ). Hints Many tsunamis, again and again, for just one gulf? Yep, that's just how life goes. Gulfs are in high demand, but you'll need many tsunamis to create just one.

meaningMnemonic: Your foot heard an omen and now it's making you hop over things. Hints Imagine your foot hearing this omen, "If you step on a crack, you'll break your mother's back." Now your foot hops over all of the tiny cracks in the street and the sidewalk and you look really silly.
readingMnemonic: As you hop you start to hear an awful scream coming down the street. It's Mrs. Chou ( ちょう ) and she's running straight for you yelling, "STEP ON MY STREET'S CRACKS! STOP HOPPING OR YOUR MOTHER WILL NEVER BREAK HER BACK!" Hints Now you're hopping away in fear from Mrs. Chou!

meaningMnemonic: Take your fingers and wrap them around another person. This is called a hug . Just make sure you include all the stuff attached to your fingers, like your hands and arms too, otherwise it's more of a squeeze, and we don't want to do that to people. Hints Picture it like you're a baby who is new to hugs. You start with your fingers, spread them out and move forward. Now wrap all that stuff attached to your fingers around another person. You did it! You're hugging now!
readingMnemonic: Who do you love to hug the most? Your da d ( だ )! He gives the best hugs. They're warm and big and tight and comforting. The kind of hug dads are really good at giving. Hints Imagine getting a nice, big hug from your dad. Mm. It's cozy and feels like home.

meaningMnemonic: When a prison holds the sun inside it, everything will always be in season . Obviously if the sun is in prison, the seasons can't change. Want to eat perfect apples all year round? readingMnemonic: When things are in season for more than ten days , people are going to wonder what's going on. When's Christmas? When's Golden Week? Soon ( しゅん ), you say. Soon June will end and people will forget about everything else, living forever inside that period of ten days when apples are most in season.

meaningMnemonic: When your ear is cross ed with sound, it catches it like a net , and sends it to your heart for processing. Hints Imagine the whole process of sound going through your ear and to your heart, then the gears turning to really understand what someone is saying. It's a real listen, not a fake non-heart listen.
readingMnemonic: You are listen ing so well to what someone is saying. What are they telling you that is so important? They are telling you of the omen of Mrs. Chou ( ちょう ), who will destroy the earth. Hints Focus on listening, and focus on their message about Mrs. Chou. Feel afraid about the future because of it.

meaningMnemonic: You give your servant a gun along with some other products to look to . You can’t look to them yourself since you are very busy. meaningMnemonic: The omen radical and the omen kanji are the same! Hints If you know the omen radical, you know the omen kanji as well!

Hints You can clarify with the person telling you the omen several things: "Do you believe in the omen about Mrs. Chou destroying the world?" "When will this omen about Mrs. Chou come true?" etc. As long as you're associating omen with Mrs. Chou you should be good, so keep harping on that. Anyway, whenever you hear any kind of omen (omen is a radical in the kanji), there's a good chance it's going to be about Mrs. Chou.

readingMnemonic: I will punish you by taking away your ca ke ( けい )! You'll never eat cake again. Not for birthdays, not for holidays. This is your punishment. meaningMnemonic: A greenhouse is the newest power of the city you decided to recruit . You’re trying to recruit all the buildings in town and the greenhouse was the next on your list. meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. In historical contexts, 陣 refers to an army camp or to the formation s soldiers used on the battlefield, often in relation to samurai battles. Sometimes, it can even mean the battle itself when you see it in the battle's name. In modern Japanese, that older sense lives on in sports, where 陣 can mean one team's side of the field. More commonly, though, 陣 is used as a suffix for a group of people with a shared affiliation, like 報道陣 (press corps) or 教授陣 (faculty).
readingMnemonic: The reading is the same as what you learned with the kanji.

meaningMnemonic: This army camp is really well manage d. Sure, it's still an army camp , but it's a really darn good one! 陣 and 陣営 both mean "army camp" when used literally, but in modern Japanese 陣営 is also often used to refer to competing camp s or faction s in politics, business, or sports.

meaningMnemonic: You are favor ed with know ing things. You have wisdom and intelligence .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word, which usually means on'yomi readings from the kanji. You didn't learn 知 's on'yomi when you learned the kanji, so here's a mnemonic to help you: Your wisdom tells you people should eat chee se ( ち ) on a regular basis. Yes, in your infinite wisdom, you know that a calcium-rich food like cheese is just what humanity needs. It is your duty, O wise one, to share this wisdom with others. Go forth! Spread the wisdom of cheese consumption with all mankind!

meaningMnemonic: You learned that 執 means "tenacious," but it can also mean " carry out ." So what do you carry out with a writing brush ? You carry out writing ! But not just any writing — this is professional writing , so you better get it right! 執筆 is a formal word for the act of writing, especially professional or important work like novels, magazine columns, news articles, or academic papers.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi reading of the kanji, but both readings are slightly altered: しつ gets shorted to しっ , and ひつ gets rendaku'd to ぴつ . If you're having trouble with the rendaku, just imagine fervently writing page after page until your pits ( ぴつ ) start to reek. Mmm, smell those musky pits. That's the smell of someone who's just poured their heart and sweat out onto the page!

meaningMnemonic: A valuable formal name ender . It's like saying "the valuable great you"... or something. Anyways, this means you , but it isn't as nice as it sounds. 貴様 used to be a polite way to say "you," but in modern Japanese it's almost always a strong insult, roughly like saying you bastard . The tone is dramatic, so you'll hear it from anime villains, but not usually in real conversation unless someone's joking around and pretending to be Vegeta from Dragon Ball.
readingMnemonic: The readings are the reading you learned with 貴 plus the vocab reading for 様 .
